title: Retrospective evaluation of joint aspirates from native and endoprosthetically treated joints
summary: It is assumed that the laboratory and cytological parameters obtained during routine clinical joint aspiration are associated with the presence of a septic process, defined by the detection of microbiological pathogens in the joint aspirate. Furthermore, it is assumed that prior antibiotic therapy is associated with a lower rate of microbiological pathogen detection. This study will exploratoryly investigate whether there is a correlation between the microbiological results of joint aspiration and intraoperatively obtained samples if surgery was performed.

interventions.name:
No study-specific examinations or interventions will be performed. Data will be collected retrospectively from electronic medical records of patients who underwent diagnostic joint aspiration as part of routine clinical care between 2015 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The data collected retrospectively consists of findings from diagnostic joint aspirations obtained as part of routine clinical practice. These include biochemical, cytological, and microbiological parameters of the synovial fluid, as determined by standard procedures and documented in the patient’s medical record.
In addition, information from the patient record (from the KAS) regarding the detection of microbiological pathogens in the synovial fluid, prior antibiotic therapy, intraoperative samples, 
as well as the clinical course and outcome (e.g., revision surgeries, mortality) is collected.
The study period covers the years 2015 through 2025
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who have previously received antibiotic therapy
Patients who have undergone multiple revisions
